doc.title: Chico Hamilton — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Package tours and the original quintet
title: Quintet instrumentation, original repertoire, and signing with Pacific Jazz
summary: He explains hearing the French horn and cello sound, that the band began with all original material, and that radio fame brought a Pacific Jazz contract and national press.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: Yeah, making you famous. So the original quintet was going to be Jim Hall on guitar, your drums, Carson -­
Carson Smith on bass and Buddy Colette on reed.
On reed, and a French horn.
And a French horn.
Now that would have been really -- wait a minute, how did you hear French horn in this?
Well I heard it. I heard the sound. You know, I know what French horns sound like.
French horn and flute or sax.
Yeah, right. Plus the fact I knew how this guy played. He could play, he could get a good sound, you know.
So I know when you started recording, you started recording a lot of your own tunes but you had to start somewhere. You didn’t start with original material? Did you start doing some -­
What’s that?
The band, the repertoire for the band.
We all started with original stuff.
That was it.
That was it.
Just figured, we’ve got an original group, original sound, we’re just going for original material.
Yeah.
No wonder you’ve made history. (Unintelligible).
Right.
Okay, so you became a hit because of the radio broadcast initially.
Yeah.
And you get a recording contract.
Right.
You’re on Atlantic.
No, I’m on Pacific Jazz.
Pacific Jazz. Then Bud came and said (unintelligible).
Yeah. (Unintelligible) regretted it too, you know.
Yeah. So now you’ve got your band. You’re documenting -- you already did the trio, now you’ve got -- and this is a successful band.
Got the original quintet.
Are you starting to get national press for this now?
